;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**Eastern-based forces of [[Khalifa Haftar]]'s [[Libyan National Army]] (LNA) say they have killed Abu Moaz al-Iraqi, leader of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant in Libya|ISIL in Libya]], in the [[Libyan Desert|desert]] city of [[Sebha]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/eastern-libyan-forces-say-they-killed-islamic-state-leader-idUSKCN26E3BW?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Timeline of terrorism in Egypt (2013–present)|Terrorism in Egypt]]
**Three [[Egypt]]ian [[Egyptian National Police|police]] officers and four convicted [[terrorist]]s on [[death row]] are killed during a failed attempt to escape from [[Tora Prison]] in [[Cairo]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-egypt-prison/three-egyptian-policemen-four-militants-killed-in-prison-break-attempt-idUKKCN26E355?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[List of explosions]]
**A [[fuel tanker]] explodes on a highway in [[Kogi State]], [[Nigeria]], destroying several nearby vehicles and killing at least 25 people. The victims include a number of [[Kogi State Polytechnic]] students whose school bus was destroyed in the blast. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-54262443 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****The number of deaths in [[India]] exceeds 90,000. In the past 24 hours, the country reported 83,347 new cases and 1,085 more deaths. [https://nation.com.pk/23-Sep-2020/total-covid-19-death-toll-crosses-90k-in-india (''The Nation PK'')] [https://www.deccanherald.com/national/indias-covid-19-tally-crosses-56-lakh-mark-with-83347-new-cases-death-toll-tops-90000-891705.html (''Deccan Herald'')]
****[[Ministry of Railways (India)|Railway Minister]] [[Suresh Angadi]] dies from the disease at the [[All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi| All India Institute of Medical Sciences]] in [[New Delhi]]. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/coronavirus-indias-railways-minister-suresh-angadi-dies-from-covid-19 (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reports a record jump of 6,923 new cases in the past 24 hours, as the country imposes a second nationwide lockdown to prevent the spread of the virus. Further restrictions are being considered. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/9/23/israel-sees-highest-ever-daily-spike-in-coronavirus-infections (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
***The number of cases in the [[Netherlands]] surpasses 100,000, after a record of 2,357 new cases is reported in the last 24 hours. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/2020/09/coronavirus-cases-top-100000-in-the-netherlands-more-regional-measures-likely/ (Dutch News)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Johnson & Johnson]] enters a Phase III clinical trial for its potential vaccine, becoming the fourth vaccine company backed by [[Operation Warp Speed]] to do so. The trial is expected to enroll up to 60,000 volunteers across 215 locations in the [[United States]] and other countries. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/23/coronavirus-vaccine-johnson-johnson-begins-late-stage-covid-19-trial-.html (CNBC)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[List of border incidents involving North and South Korea]]
***The [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|South Korean defense ministry]] alleges that [[North Korea]]n officials killed and [[Cremation|cremated]] an official from the [[Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries|South Korean fisheries ministry]] who disappeared from a ship conducting [[maritime patrol]] activities along the [[Northern Limit Line]] on September 21 and entered North Korean territory by the following afternoon. [https://spectrumnews1.com/oh/cincinnati/ap-online/2020/09/24/seoul-north-korea-fired-at-a-s-korean-and-burned-his-body (AP via NY1)]
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]]
**[[King of Saudi Arabia|King]] [[Salman of Saudi Arabia]] calls for a "comprehensive and firm" response to [[government of Iran|Iran]]'s [[nuclear program of Iran|nuclear program]] and condemns what he describes as "its expansionist activities, create its terrorist networks, and use terrorism", adding that it produces nothing but "chaos, extremism, and sectarianism". An Iranian official rebuffs the accusations as "baseless". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/9/23/saudi-king-calls-for-comprehensive-solution-on-iran-in-un-speech (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mexico–United States relations]], [[Immigration detention in the United States]]
**[[Mexico]] is investigating claims that six [[Mexicans|Mexican]] women were [[Compulsory sterilization#United States|sterilised]] while in a [[Immigration detention in the United States|migrant detention center]], says Foreign Minister [[Marcelo Ebrard]]. A [[whistleblower]] the previous week alleged [[hysterectomies]] were being performed on immigrants in the United States without their proper consent. Mexico called such operations "unacceptable". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-54265571 (BBC News)]
*[[Foreign relations of Argentina]]
**[[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] demands Iran extradite the Iranian citizens accused of responsibility for the 1994 [[AMIA bombing]] in Buenos Aires and states that the demand is of "vital importance". [https://www.telam.com.ar/notas/202009/517233-la-amia-destaco-el-reclamo-de-fernandez-a-iran-ante-la-onu-para-esclarecer-el-atentado-de-1994.html (Argentine Official News Agency Télam)]
*[[Belarus–United States relations]], [[International reactions to the 2020 Belarusian presidential election and protests]]
**The [[United States]] formally no longer recognizes [[Alexander Lukashenko]] as [[President of Belarus]], according to a [[United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State]] statement. A State Department spokesperson calls for a new "free and fair election" in Belarus under independent observation. [https://www.axios.com/us-lukashenko-president-belarus-353ed235-98f7-446f-919a-6a6cdab81975.html (''Axios'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Shooting of Breonna Taylor]]
**A grand jury in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], indicts former [[Louisville Metro Police Department|police]] officer Brett Hankison on felony charges of wanton [[endangerment]] for firing into a neighboring apartment, but no officers are charged directly with Breonna Taylor's death. A large police presence is seen in Louisville as protests continue. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/09/23/kentucky-grand-jury-breonna-taylor-brett-hankison-charged/3467413001/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.cnn.com/us/live-news/breonna-taylor-announcement/index.html (CNN)]
**Two [[Louisville Metro Police Department|Louisville Metro Police]] officers are shot and wounded during protests over the Breonna Taylor indictment. One suspect is reportedly in custody. [https://apnews.com/28a283922de8784f6fca5c42fe8e5bca (AP)]
**After the city declared a state of emergency, [[Governor of Kentucky|Governor]] [[Andy Beshear]] sends the [[Kentucky Army National Guard]] to Louisville in response to the protests. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/517905-kentucky-governor-authorizes-national-guard-as-protesters-gather-over (''The Hill'')]
*[[LGBT rights in the Cook Islands]]
**[[Human rights]] campaigners urge [[Cook Islands]]' MPs to abolish Article 64 of the Crimes Act, which criminalises [[gay]] men with up to 14 years' imprisonment. The activists call on the lawmakers to abide by the Constitution. The Cook Islands is a sovereign territory belonging to [[New Zealand]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/426741/human-rights-campaigners-urge-cook-island-mps-to-uphold-constitution (RNZ)]
*[[Hong Kong]] [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy camp]] activist [[Joshua Wong]] loses a court case against his disqualification from running in last year's November election. The returning officer had disqualified him because she did not believe Wong had changed his stance on [[Hong Kong independence]] and his "subversive intentions". [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3102666/hong-kong-opposition-activist-joshua-wong-loses-legal (''South China Morning Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Belarusian presidential election]], [[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[President of Belarus|President]] Alexander Lukashenko is sworn in for a sixth term in office at an unannounced inauguration at the [[Independence Palace, Minsk|Independence Palace]] in [[Minsk]]. The opposition and some foreign governments do not recognize the legitimacy of the inauguration, and call for continued [[civil resistance]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-54262953 (BBC News)]
*[[Death and funeral of Ruth Bader Ginsburg]]
**Deceased [[Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States|Associate Justice]] [[Ruth Bader Ginsburg]] [[Lying in repose|lies in repose]] in the [[United States Supreme Court Building]]. She is both the first woman and the first [[Jewish American]] to receive such an honor. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54271027?at_campaign=64& (BBC News)]
*[[2020 United States presidential election]], [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] refuses to commit to a peaceful [[United States presidential transition|transfer of power]] if he loses the November 3 presidential election, saying "We're going to have to see what happens". [https://apnews.com/8bb28627b03474a3a5ce2454ae3d1639?utm_campaign=SocialFlow&utm_medium=AP&utm_source=Twitter (AP)]
*[[Ishmael Toroama]] is declared President-elect of the [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville]] following an election process that began six weeks ago. Toroama secured 48,766 votes cast and promised to solve the issue of independence. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/426722/ishmael-toroama-declared-president-elect-of-bougainville (RNZ)] 

;Science and technology
*Astronomers announce the crescent shadow of [[Messier 87]]'s [[supermassive black hole]] is wobbling. Back in April 2019, the [[Event Horizon Telescope]] captured the crescent shadow of the [[Messier 87#Supermassive black hole M87*|black hole]], making it the first image ever taken of a black hole.  [http://www.sci-news.com/astronomy/wobbling-crescent-shadow-messier-87-supermassive-black-hole-08880.html (Sci News)]
*Archaeologists discover some [[Stainless steel|chromium crucible steel (stainless steel)]] that was first made in [[Iran|Persia]] as early as the [[11th century]]. [http://www.sci-news.com/archaeology/chromium-crucible-steel-persia-08879.html (Sci News)]
